subQuestion.ans: (i) 4/5 is an element of the set Q (ii) -2 is not an element of the set N (iii) Set P is a set of all p's such that p is an odd number

questions.questionsTitle: Practice Set 1.2 - Equal Sets, Empty Sets, and Finite/Infinite Sets

subQuestion.question: Decide which of the following are equal sets and which are not. Justify your answer: (i) A = {x | 3x - 1 = 2} (ii) B = {x | x is a natural number but x is neither prime nor composite} (iii) C = {x | x ∈ N, x < 2}
subQuestion.ans: All three sets A, B, and C are equal sets. (i) A = {1} because 3x - 1 = 2 gives x = 1 (ii) B = {1} because 1 is the only natural number that is neither prime nor composite (iii) C = {1} because 1 is the only natural number less than 2. Since all sets contain the same element (1), they are equal sets.

subQuestion.question: Decide whether sets A and B are equal sets or not. Give reason for your answer: (i) A = {Even prime numbers} (ii) B = {x | 7x - 1 = 13}
subQuestion.ans: Sets A and B are equal sets. (i) A = {2} because 2 is the only even prime number (ii) B = {2} because solving 7x - 1 = 13 gives x = 2. Since both sets contain the same element (2), they are equal sets.

subQuestion.question: Which of the following sets are empty sets? Why? (i) A = {a | a is a natural number smaller than zero} (ii) B = {x | x² = 0} (iii) C = {x | 5x - 2 = 0, x ∈ N}
subQuestion.ans: (i) A is an empty set because there is no natural number smaller than zero (ii) B is not an empty set because x² = 0 gives x = 0, so B = {0} (iii) C is an empty set because 5x - 2 = 0 gives x = 2/5, which is not a natural number

subQuestion.question: Write with reasons, which of the following sets are finite or infinite: (i) A = {x | x < 10, x is a natural number} (ii) B = {y | y < -1, y is an integer} (iii) C = Set of students of class 9 from your school (iv) Set of people from your village (v) Set of apparatus in laboratory (vi) Set of whole numbers (vii) Set of rational numbers
subQuestion.ans: Finite sets: (i) A = {1, 2, ..., 8, 9} - countable elements (iii) C - countable number of students (iv) countable number of people (v) limited apparatus. Infinite sets: (ii) B = {..., -4, -3, -2} - extends infinitely (vi) whole numbers continue infinitely (vii) infinite rational numbers exist

questions.questionsTitle: Practice Set 1.3 - Subsets, Complements, and Venn Diagrams

subQuestion.question: If A = {a, b, c, d, e}, B = {c, d, e, f}, C = {b, d}, D = {a, e}, then which of the following statements are true and which are false? (i) C ⊆ B (ii) A ⊆ D (iii) D ⊆ B (iv) D ⊆ A (v) B ⊆ A (vi) C ⊆ A
subQuestion.ans: (i) False - Element b of set C is not in set B (ii) False - All elements of set A are not in set D (iii) False - Element a of set D is not in set B (iv) True - Elements a and e both of set D are also in set A (v) False - Element f of set B is not in set A (vi) True - Elements b and d both of set C are in set A

subQuestion.question: Take the set of natural numbers from 1 to 20 as universal set and show sets X and Y using Venn diagram: (i) X = {x | x ∈ N, and 7 < x < 15} (ii) Y = {y | y ∈ N, y is a prime number from 1 to 20}
U = {1, 2, 3, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12}, P = {1, 3, 7, 10}. (i) Show the sets U, P and P' by Venn diagram (ii) Verify: (P')' = P
A = {1, 3, 2, 7}, write three subsets of set A
subQuestion.ans: Three subsets of A can be: {1}, {1, 3}, {2, 7} (Note: Any three subsets from the 16 possible subsets can be written)

subQuestion.question: Write the subset relation between the sets: P (residents of Pune), M (residents of Madhya Pradesh), I (residents of Indore), B (residents of India), H (residents of Maharashtra). Which set can be chosen as the universal set?
subQuestion.ans: Subset relations: P ⊆ H, P ⊆ B, I ⊆ M, I ⊆ B, M ⊆ B, H ⊆ B. The set B (residents of India) can be chosen as the universal set since all other sets are subsets of B.

subQuestion.question: Which set of numbers could be the universal set for the given sets? (i) A = multiples of 5, B = multiples of 7, C = multiples of 12 (ii) P = integers which are multiples of 4, T = all even square numbers
subQuestion.ans: (i) Any of the sets N (natural numbers), W (whole numbers), or I (integers) can be the universal set (ii) Any of the sets N, W, or I can be the universal set for sets P and T

subQuestion.question: Let all students of a class be the universal set. Let set A be students who secure 50% or more marks in Maths. Write the complement of set A.
subQuestion.ans: A' = {The set of students who secured less than 50% marks in Maths}
